targetObserved: pay BFF adds /status but reads intent
frontend and pay microservice routes absent
pay service GET /api/v1/pay/history/{address} trusts path address
frontend exposes unrelated canned subscription routes
inbox insert and state update are non-atomic

ownershipRules.rule: payer, payment owner, status and history scope derive only from the verified JWT wallet; body/path wallet fields never grant ownership
receiver, token, chain, amount, currency, plan price and eligibility derive from server configuration and durable plan records
authenticated reads of foreign owner-scoped resources return the same 404 as missing resources
payment and escrow admin mutations require admin audience and admin:payments:manage
plan mutation requires admin audience and admin:plans:manage
reads are participant scoped; release is payer-or-admin, refund payee-or-admin, dispute either participant, resolve admin-or-configured-arbitrator

idempotencyRules.rule: Idempotency-Key is scoped by verified principal and operation and persists request hash plus original response
same key and body returns the recorded response; same key with a different body returns 409
payment submission is unique on chain_id and tx_hash; chain event identity is unique on chain_id, tx_hash and log_index
state transitions compare expected state, require exactly one affected row, and atomically write aggregate, audit, inbox/outbox and entitlement changes

finalityRules.rule: backend verifies configured chain, successful receipt and canonical block identity
backend verifies supported token and exact Transfer sender, receiver and amount; browser receipt alone is insufficient
chain policy controls finality; compatibility baseline is 15 confirmations on BSC mainnet and 3 off-mainnet
block hash, block number and log index are persisted; reorgs before finality cannot activate payment, escrow, subscription or plan access

nonProductionSurfaces.reason: Hard-coded plans, payment amount/status and subscription records are not durable financial state.
Redirecting the legacy payment page does not prove quote, wallet, submit, poll or activation compatibility.
The BFF route calls a nonexistent execute endpoint and defaults missing payer/payee to the zero address.
The success path renders confirmation copy without reading a verified terminal backend state.
Runtime DDL and unverified split state changes are not a production migration or on-chain escrow implementation.
Immediate activation and a zero vault address do not prove funded recurring access.
Force operations and empty mutation bodies lack the downstream authorization and typed execution proof.

durableStateDependencies: one declared payment and subscription write authority
versioned reversible migrations with foreign keys checks and unique chain identities
principal-scoped idempotency key and request hash store
atomic aggregate audit inbox outbox and entitlement transaction
receipt transfer block hash block number log index and confirmation evidence
unique active subscription and explicit period lifecycle constraints
cutover backfill reconciliation rollback and orphan-recovery ledgers
deploymentDependencies: public pay hostname terminates at the authenticated BFF while raw services remain private
gateway prefix rewrites and method policies are parity tested
subscription service has a reviewed deployment and health/readiness configuration
escrow vault receiver and token addresses are nonzero per-chain reviewed configuration
webhook caller has rotatable service identity and key material
reconciliation monitoring alerting and operator runbooks are installed before cutover

blockers.summary: Rust frontend lacks source-compatible payment APIs and returns canned plan/subscription/payment data.
blockers.resolution: Implement compatibility handlers backed by the declared write authority; remove canned financial responses.

blockers.summary: The frontend redirects to a pay host whose BFF checkout is not a verified executable wallet flow.
blockers.resolution: Wire quote, wallet transaction, backend submission, polling and verified terminal screens end to end.

blockers.summary: pay.epsx.io tunnel reaches the pay service NodePort rather than the pay BFF described by its comment.
blockers.resolution: Choose and test the public BFF service/NodePort route; keep the raw service private.

blockers.summary: Gateway mounts /api/v1/payment while the service uses /api/v1/pay and deliberately blocks financial routing.
blockers.resolution: Lock one prefix or an explicit rewrite with exact method and ownership tests.

blockers.summary: Pay BFF singular routes call a nonexistent service execute endpoint instead of the service confirm endpoint.
blockers.resolution: Implement typed, authenticated compatibility calls and exact response/status mapping.

blockers.summary: Pay service trusts caller payer/payee/address data and exposes owner-unscoped reads and mutations.
blockers.resolution: Enforce verified owner keys at gateway and service and server-authoritative payment coordinates.

blockers.summary: Admin BFF route/body contracts drift; empty confirm/release bodies cannot satisfy downstream models and service permissions are absent.
blockers.resolution: Lock typed admin DTOs and enforce admin audience plus operation permissions downstream.

blockers.summary: Financial mutations have no request idempotency and confirm performs split non-transactional writes.
blockers.resolution: Add idempotency records, request hashes, compare-and-set transitions and atomic inbox/outbox transactions.

blockers.summary: Pay confirm accepts any nonempty transaction hash without receipt, Transfer, amount, receiver, token or finality verification.
blockers.resolution: Reuse or port canonical receipt/Transfer verification and persist reorg/finality evidence before activation.

blockers.summary: Escrow operations are DB status changes with unproven participant/admin authority, transition guards and on-chain execution.
blockers.resolution: Lock participant permissions, contract configuration, signed/on-chain execution, CAS transitions and reconciliation.

blockers.summary: Webhook uses body HMAC and event_id dedupe but lacks service identity, timestamp replay window and atomic state application.
blockers.resolution: Require service identity plus key ID/timestamp/digest and atomically apply chain-event inbox, transition and outbox.

blockers.summary: Subscription CRUD trusts caller identity and activates immediately without payment/finality/vault verification.
blockers.resolution: Derive owner/admin identity, require finalized funding, add period and uniqueness constraints, and remove zero/canned vault data.

blockers.summary: Pay and subscription services create tables at runtime without versioned migration constraints or an outbox.
blockers.resolution: Create reviewed, reversible migrations with FKs, checks, uniqueness, audit, idempotency and inbox/outbox tables.

blockers.summary: Canonical backend and extracted services have independent payment/subscription write models with no cutover or reconciliation contract.
blockers.resolution: Declare one write authority, migration/backfill, reconciliation, rollback and retirement sequence.

blockers.summary: Route prefixes, verbs, request DTOs, envelopes and success/error statuses are not parity-locked.
blockers.resolution: Add typed contract fixtures for every route and lock the status semantics in this contract.

blockers.summary: No complete replay, reorg, recovery, reconciliation, browser, service authorization or financial observability proof exists.
blockers.resolution: Add deterministic tests and production-shaped metrics/alerts/runbooks without using production in the gate.

blockers.summary: Subscription deployment is absent from the audited infrastructure and pay escrow contract remains a zero placeholder.
blockers.resolution: Add reviewed non-placeholder configuration and deployment manifests only after execution and authorization proofs pass.

safety.readinessMeaning: STOP until every blocker has reviewed implementation evidence
